abstract: NBER working paper analyzing ChatGPT usage patterns among approximately 700 million users, finding that 81% of work-related use is for decision support rather than content generation or task automation. The study provides the largest-scale analysis of how workers actually use generative AI, revealing that the dominant use case is informing human decisions rather than replacing human work -- a pattern with significant implications for AI's labor market impact.
keyFindings: ChatGPT has approximately 700 million users globally
81% of work-related usage is for decision support, not content generation or automation
Decision support usage suggests AI is primarily augmenting rather than replacing human judgment
Usage patterns indicate AI's labor impact may be more subtle than wholesale task automation
methodology: NBER working paper analyzing large-scale ChatGPT usage data to categorize work-related use cases and measure the share of usage devoted to decision support versus other functions.
qualifiers: Usage data may not capture all AI tool usage beyond ChatGPT. Decision support and automation exist on a spectrum and categorization involves judgment calls. High decision-support share may reflect current AI limitations rather than stable user preferences.
